items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: My two uncles taught me how to play and they told me who to listen to

ctx.x: Did you come from a musical family? Because I know your family now is pretty darned musical.

Oh yes. My two uncles taught me how to play and they told me who to listen to, you know, Benny Goodman’s band and George Van Eps and Alan Reuss and Charlie Christian. But they happened to be very good. My older uncle, Peter Domenick, had a day job so he never thought of going on the road but was very capable of playing with any band in those days. He was an expert banjo player. And my younger uncle, Bobby, did go on the road with Bob Chester, Raymond Scott, Buddy Rodgers, dance bands, playing rhythm guitar.
So you were a teenager in the early 40s? You were born in ‘26?

items.title: Ruth & Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Saddle River, New Jersey, January 19, 2015
items.q: I had my uncles show me, and I knew the good musicians in Paterson, and I learned from them more than anybody else.

ctx.x: I had my uncles show me, and I knew the good musicians in Paterson, and I learned from them more than anybody else.
Do you think that can still happen these days?
